nodes.label: Markdown Lint Workflow
nodes.rationale: Markdown and markdown-extension files are linted on pushes and pull requests targeting master.

nodes.label: PDD Workflow
nodes.rationale: The pdd-action checks puzzle-driven-development annotations on master changes.

nodes.label: Typos Workflow
nodes.rationale: crate-ci typos checks repository text on master pushes and pull requests.

nodes.label: actionlint Workflow
nodes.rationale: Pushes and pull requests against master are checked with reviewdog's actionlint integration on Ubuntu 24.04.

nodes.label: Yamllint Workflow
nodes.rationale: YAML files are checked with ibiqlik/action-yamllint on master pushes and pull requests.

nodes.label: bashate Workflow
nodes.rationale: Shell scripts are discovered and linted with bashate under Python 3.14, explicitly ignoring E006 and E003.

nodes.label: ShellCheck Workflow
nodes.rationale: Shell source is statically checked with the action-shellcheck integration on master changes.

nodes.label: XCOP Workflow
nodes.rationale: The xcop-named master workflow currently defines only repository checkout.

nodes.label: Active-Element Iteration
nodes.rationale: Iterators scale with M, the number of stored elements, instead of the full configured capacity.

nodes.label: Constant-Time next_key Allocation
nodes.rationale: next_key selects an available usize key in O(1) time.

nodes.label: emap Map
nodes.rationale: The crate models a fixed-capacity associative array with usize keys, aiming for HashMap-like ergonomics and much lower overhead for its constrained use case.

nodes.label: Fixed-Capacity Performance Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: Capacity must be known up front and overflow panics because avoiding automatic growth is explicitly identified as one source of speed.

nodes.label: IntMap Benchmark Results
nodes.rationale: The May 2025 benchmark reports strong emap gains for small capacities and several operations, while some scan-heavy cases fall below IntMap at larger capacities.

nodes.label: Per-Element Memory Overhead
nodes.rationale: The data structure requires an explicitly documented overhead of two usize values per capacity slot.

nodes.label: Rultor Merge Quality Gate
nodes.rationale: Merge automation requires verbose tests, rustfmt checking, documentation generation, and Clippy without dependency linting.

nodes.label: Semantic-Version Release Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Release tags must match a three-part semantic version before version substitution, all-feature tests, formatting, Clippy, version commit, credential installation, and cargo publish.

nodes.label: Benchmark Workflow
nodes.rationale: The master-only benchmark job currently checks out the repository but defines no benchmark execution step.

nodes.label: Cargo Workflow
nodes.rationale: Push and pull-request runs are deduplicated by ref with cancellation, although the build job currently performs checkout only.

nodes.label: Copyrights Workflow
nodes.rationale: The copyrights action checks license, build, shell, YAML, Rust, and numerous other source-file globs for copyright headers.

nodes.label: REUSE Workflow
nodes.rationale: The FSFE REUSE action validates machine-readable licensing compliance on master pushes and pull requests.

nodes.label: Tarpaulin Workflow
nodes.rationale: The coverage-named workflow runs on pushes and pull requests but currently contains only repository checkout.

nodes.label: Up Workflow
nodes.rationale: The workflow triggers for master and every tag but currently performs checkout only.

nodes.label: MIT License
nodes.rationale: The license permits use, modification, distribution, sublicensing, and sale while requiring preservation of the notice and disclaiming warranty and liability.

nodes.label: REUSE MIT License Copy
nodes.rationale: The LICENSES directory contains the same MIT grant, notice condition, and warranty disclaimer for REUSE-compatible license discovery.

nodes.label: Rultor Configuration
nodes.rationale: Rultor uses a Rust container and secured crates.io credentials to gate merges and publish releases.

nodes.label: Performance Regression Contribution Gate
nodes.rationale: Contributors are instructed to benchmark before and after changes and reconsider submissions that degrade performance, in addition to tests, rustfmt, and Clippy.
